title: Client shim roadmap for windowed streaming, checkpointed pagination, and idempotent retries
creator: Aisha Nair
description: Public PRD describing a cross-language client shim and SDK guidelines to support windowed (frame-based) streaming, checkpointed pagination, and strong retry semantics for Python/TS/Go clients. Goal: let product teams adopt newer streaming semantics and resume semantics without breaking existing customers and to provide clear compatibility guarantees across minor server changes.
background: Recent customer incidents showed resumed streaming use-cases fail when the server rotates model variants or when tokenized cursors include internal pointers. Multiple SDKs have diverged in how they represent streaming boundaries, resume tokens, and retry idempotency. This PRD consolidates requirements, compatibility rules, and acceptance criteria so engineering and DX can deliver a single shim and set of API patterns that SDKs adopt.
requirements: REQ-001: Pagination tokens MUST be opaque to clients and include a stable server_version identifier and an expiry timestamp encoded; clients must treat tokens as single binary/string values and avoid parsing them.

REQ-002: Checkpoint tokens for streams MUST include frame_cursor and server_version and support 'seek' semantics: clients can pass a checkpoint to resume from the next frame. Servers may return an 'invalid_checkpoint' error if token expired or incompatible.

REQ-003: Frame-based streaming semantics: streams are delivered as discrete 'frames' (logical units) with optional metadata headers. Each frame has a monotonically increasing frame_index within a stream session.

REQ-004: Windowed streaming: clients should request a 'frame_window' (integer) controlling maximum frames delivered per package/batch; servers will respect but may deliver fewer. Default frame_window is 8.

REQ-005: Retry semantics: clients MUST use idempotency keys for non-read-only operations. For streaming/resume operations, clients SHOULD attach an idempotency key to the initial session request so server can deduplicate session creation on retries.

REQ-006: Backwards compatibility: minor server versions MUST continue to accept prior pagination tokens for at least 30 days after new token format rollout with a recommended deprecation notice in response metadata.

REQ-007: SDKs (Python/TS/Go) MUST export a minimal shim layer that: 1) normalizes streaming events into an AsyncIterator (TS/Python) or channel-like consumer (Go); 2) exposes a resume(checkpoint) method; 3) implements transparent retry with configurable policy.

REQ-008: Error model: server error codes include invalid_checkpoint, expired_checkpoint, incompatible_version, transient, permanent. SDKs must surface these as typed exceptions or error classes per language idioms.
REQ-009: Observability: SDKs must emit telemetry hooks for: checkpoint issued, resume attempted, retry attempted, stream frame dropped, and token expiry encountered.
REQ-010: Migration: SDKs should provide a 'compatibility mode' flag that when enabled will keep older cursor/pagination helpers around and emit deprecation warnings for one release cycle.
REQ-011: Retry backoff: Default retry policy for transient errors: initial_delay=200ms, multiplier=2.0, max_delay=5s, max_attempts=5. Policy must be configurable by the integrator.
REQ-012: Memory safety: streaming iterators must apply bounded buffering (default 64 frames) and provide a backpressure callback to the application.
REQ-013: Tests: Each SDK must include an integration test suite that validates resume with mocked expiry, invalid tokens, and minor server-version skew scenarios.
REQ-014: Documentation: Provide migration guide, API reference for checkpoint tokens, and code examples for Python/TS/Go illustrating resume and idempotency usage.
REQ-015: Security: Checkpoint tokens MUST be encrypted-signed by server; SDKs must treat them as secrets and avoid logging full token values by default.
non_functional: NFR-001: Latency: resuming a stream using a valid checkpoint should not add more than 15ms server-side median overhead compared to cold start for same model.
NFR-002: Stability: SDK shim must be fully backwards compatible for existing clients unless compatibility_mode=false; deprecation warnings should be non-disruptive.
NFR-003: Resource usage: default buffering and window sizes should be conservative to avoid client memory spikes (see REQ-012).
NFR-004: Cross-language parity: Feature surface must be functionally equivalent in Python/TS/Go within ergonomics of each language.
NFR-005: Test coverage: unit+integration for shim >=90% coverage for code paths implementing resume and retries.
api_examples:
Python example:
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="REDACTED")
# start streaming session
session = client.start_stream(prompt="read log", frame_window=8, idempotency_key="sess-123")
for frame in session.async_iter():
    process(frame)
# save checkpoint to resume later
checkpoint = session.checkpoint
# resume
resumed = client.resume_stream(checkpoint=checkpoint)
for frame in resumed.async_iter():
    process(frame)
compatibility_matrix:
Matrix row: server_minor_v -> client_compat_behavior:
- v1.x (before rollout): accept old_token; no checkpoint support.
- v1.x+1 (rollout): support old_token + new_checkpoint; servers return metadata 'deprecated_token' when old token used.
- v1.x+2 (removal planned): old_token accepted for 30 days then rejected with 'incompatible_version'.
SDK guidance: Ship 'compatibility_mode' default=true for one release after server rollout, then warn for two releases before switching default to false.
Edge cases: If server_version in token mismatches client-supported-version, SDK must surface 'incompatible_version' and provide a helper to re-run request from scratch.
acceptance_criteria: AC-001: SDKs (Python/TS/Go) implement shim API surface with start_stream/resume_stream/session.checkpoint and pass cross-language integration tests.
AC-002: Integration test simulates server returning expired_checkpoint and SDK surfaces typed error and does not attempt infinite retries.
AC-003: Performance test: resume median overhead < 15ms in synthetic benchmark harness.
AC-004: Documentation pages (migration guide + API reference) published in docs site with examples for three languages.
AC-005: Console telemetry hooks visible in staging dashboards for checkpoint-issued and resume-attempted events.

AC-006: Compatibility mode default=true release published and deprecation warnings emitted when old tokens are used; monitoring set to alert if >1% of resumed sessions start failing due to incompatible tokens.

ENG-33105 (server-side error code additions and deprecation headers)
